title: Social Media Schema Design
description: Model users, posts, comments, likes, and follows for a social platform

data.text: Social media schemas must support high read volume, recursive relationships, and flexible engagement actions. The main challenge is balancing normalization with query performance for feeds.

data.title: Social media DDL
data.content: Design users, posts, comments, likes, and follows with recursive follow relationships.
data.code:
CREATE TABLE users (
  user_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
  username VARCHAR(64) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  email VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  bio TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE posts (
  post_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
  user_id INT NOT NULL,
  content TEXT NOT NULL,
  media_url VARCHAR(512),
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE comments (
  comment_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
  post_id INT NOT NULL,
  user_id INT NOT NULL,
  parent_comment_id INT NULL,
  content TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE likes (
  like_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
  user_id INT NOT NULL,
  post_id INT NULL,
  comment_id INT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

data.title: Warning
data.text: Polymorphic likes with nullable post_id and comment_id can cause data integrity issues. Consider separate tables or a junction table with a type column.

items.question: How do I model threaded comments?
items.answer: Use parent_comment_id for adjacency lists, or a closure table for efficient recursive queries.

items.question: Should likes be unique per user and post?
items.answer: Yes. Add a unique constraint on (user_id, post_id) and consider (user_id, comment_id) for comment likes.

items.question: How do I handle media attachments?
items.answer: Store a Media table with polymorphic references or a JSON array of URLs in the post table if attachments are lightweight.

data.title: Summary
points: Use recursive foreign keys for follows
Enforce unique likes per user and target
Separate media from post text for scalability
data.takeaway: Social schemas need recursive patterns, polymorphic actions, and strict uniqueness constraints to keep engagement data clean.
